ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The agave, or century plant, generally grows in arid climates with unpredictable rainfall and poor soil. The plant exhibits what is commonly called big bang reproduction. An agave grows for years, accumulating nutrients in its tissues until there is an unusually wet year. Then it sends up a large flowering stalk, produces seeds, and dies.

Which of the following statements gives the most likely explanation for how the agave plant has evolved this unusual life strategy?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: This particular life strategy was selected for by the harsh, desert environment.

The plant exhibits what is commonly called big bang reproduction. An agave grows for years, accumulating nutrients in its tissues until there is an unusually wet year. Then it sends up a large flowering stalk, produces seeds, and dies. What most likely selected for the agave plant's unusual life strategy?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: This particular life strategy was selected for by the harsh, desert environment.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows two life stages of agave: on the left is a plant with a leaf rosette close to the ground, with no flowers; on the right is the same low rosette-like plant, but a very tall flowering stalk grows from the center, with flowers and leaves at the upper end. This is consistent with the life history described in the question stem, “accumulating nutrients for many years, then in a wet year sending up a large flower stalk all at once, producing seeds, and dying.” The key environmental pressures given in the question stem are: agave grows in an arid climate, rainfall is unpredictable, and the soil is poor. Water and nutrients are both very limited, so if it reproduced in small amounts every year, it might not successfully produce enough seeds. Natural selection would favor those individuals that can store nutrients for many years and wait until a rare wet year to concentrate all resources into reproduction, because this strategy is more likely to successfully leave offspring in a desert environment. Therefore, the factor most likely to select for this unusual life strategy is harsh, arid desert environment with scarce water, unpredictable rainfall, and poor soil.
